text: {"overall_winner": "A", "qualities": [{"evidence": "Essay A organizes around three clear reasons (dangerous, cause problems, laziness) with a body paragraph for each and a conclusion", "quality": "Organizational structure", "description": "The essay presents a clear thesis and develops each supporting point in its own paragraph, giving the argument a coherent, easy-to-follow structure."}, {"evidence": "Essay A directly quotes the article: \"when the vehicle is in danger of backing into an object\" and \"the technology fails and some is injured, who is at fault-the driver or the manufactuer?\"", "quality": "Use of textual evidence", "description": "The essay integrates specific details and quotations from the source article to ground its claims, whereas Essay B paraphrases more loosely and less precisely."}, {"evidence": "Essay A states its position clearly in the opening: \"No, driverless cars should not be developed\" and returns to it in the conclusion", "quality": "Clear position statement", "description": "The essay announces its stance directly at the start and reaffirms it at the end, keeping the argument focused on a single, explicit position."}, {"evidence": "Essay A develops each reason with explanation, such as explaining how lawsuits and lost business would follow from technology failure", "quality": "Reason development", "description": "The essay elaborates on each of its claims with concrete consequences and reasoning rather than merely asserting them."}, {"evidence": "Essay A's conclusion weighs the opposing view (\"having driverless cars sounds pretty cool\") before reaffirming its position", "quality": "Counterpoint acknowledgment", "description": "The essay briefly acknowledges the appeal of driverless cars before dismissing it, showing some balance in the argument."}]}
